title: Verifying visible milestones on large construction sites
dek: A contractor reports that a station roof is complete. Can the owner see the full roof outline on an independently dated image? A pair of satellite observations can help an engineer decide where to send an inspector before the next payment review.

glance.label: Buyer
glance.value: An infrastructure owner, its supervising engineer or its lender. The Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) used dated imagery to follow Bengaluru Metro construction. [1]

glance.label: Decision
glance.value: Accept the visible footprint as corroborating evidence, request a clearer observation or send someone to inspect a discrepancy.

glance.label: Deliverable
glance.value: A dated image pair, the approved drawing revision and an annotated record for each disputed work area.

glance.label: First purchase
glance.value: Look for suitable archive dates. If the reporting window is still open, compare the cost and terms of a new collection. [2] [3]

problem: A progress report might call an entire station “roof complete” even though the contract treats the canopy, waterproofing and drainage as separate work packages. The owner’s engineer can ask a narrower question: was roof covering visible across the agreed footprint by the reporting date? An image can answer part of that question while a site team checks the hidden layers.

AIIB investment officers used comparisons of successive commercial images when site visits became difficult. The bank published imagery of Line R6 of the Bangalore Metro Rail Project spanning 2017–2021. Bangalore Metro Rail Corporation Limited is the implementing agency. The bank describes using the images to inform discussions with its clients and local consultants. [1] [4]

workflow.title: Define the observable milestone
workflow.text: Use the signed drawing to outline one work package, specify its due date and agree what should be visible. For paving, separate the paved surface from graded soil. For a roof, specify whether open bays count. Keep the drawing revision and site inspection date with the result.

workflow.title: Collect the reflected light
workflow.text: Sunlight reflects from the surface into a telescope. A detector converts incoming photons into an electrical signal that is digitized on board. Planet’s SkySat cameras collect a broad panchromatic band and narrower color bands. The shapes and edges in the image help an analyst locate a roof or paved apron. Color alone is a weak basis for identifying its material. [5]

workflow.title: Align the dates
workflow.text: After downlink, use radiometrically corrected, orthorectified imagery. Orthorectification uses a camera model and elevation data to place pixels on a map. Overlay both dates on stable ground features outside the work zone. Record the residual offsets and draw an uncertainty band around disputed edges. Buildings can appear to lean differently in oblique views. [5]

workflow.title: Return evidence to the engineer
workflow.text: Trace the visible change in each work package. Mask cloud, deep shadow and areas hidden by adjacent buildings. Attach the original acquisition times, visible area, obscured area and drawing revision. Send any contradiction or unobservable claim to the engineer with a specific question for the site visit.

hardware.title: Choose a camera for the feature
hardware.text: Planet documents a 3.6 m focal-length Cassegrain telescope and three CMOS imaging detectors on SkySat. Its product specification lists a 0.50 m orthorectified pixel grid and native panchromatic samples that vary by spacecraft. For example, it lists 0.65 m for SkySat-3 through -15. Pixel spacing alone cannot establish whether two adjoining roof panels can be distinguished. [5]

hardware.title: Specify the spacecraft and service
hardware.text: A dedicated or hosted camera needs stable pointing during exposure, time-tagged attitude and orbit data, a calibrated focal plane, power, thermal control, storage and a downlink sized for the planned scenes. Ask the operator to demonstrate the image quality at the largest permitted look angle and the delivery time after a successful pass. [5] [6]

hardware.title: Specify the ground delivery
hardware.text: Request image files that can be opened in the project GIS, acquisition metadata and permission to share annotated extracts with the engineer and lender. Preserve the original files. Check alignment against surveyed points where available, and compare against withheld inspection records before using the result in a progress review. [1] [5]

orbitsCompared.geometry: A low-orbit optical spacecraft sees the site during passes. An operator may point sideways to add opportunities. [5]
orbitsCompared.performance: SkySat offers submeter image products. Sentinel-2’s 10 m visible bands show broad earthworks. Daylight, clouds and competing orders limit usable dates. [2] [5] [7]
orbitsCompared.decision: Buy the archive pair whose scale, dates and viewing angles fit the signed milestone.

orbitsCompared.geometry: For the same angular pixel size, ground sampling distance grows roughly in proportion to range near nadir.
orbitsCompared.performance: A hypothetical camera ten times farther away would sample about ten times more ground per pixel with the same optics and detector. Recovering comparable detail requires a different optical system and pointing budget.
orbitsCompared.decision: Seek demonstrated image pairs from the offered system before budgeting for a MEO payload.

orbitsCompared.geometry: A geostationary satellite stays above one longitude and can repeatedly view the same region.
orbitsCompared.performance: NOAA’s ABI weather imager samples its finest visible band at 0.5 km at nadir. That is five times the length of an illustrative 100 m building in one pixel. [8]
orbitsCompared.decision: Use weather imagery to understand cloud conditions. Procure fine spatial detail separately.

costs.model: Buy existing data or order an image
costs.headline: From $300 per new 25 km² collection
costs.unit: USD · SkyFi advertised starting price, checked 24 November 2026
costs.detail: SkyFi lists 50 cm optical tasking from $300 for 25 km² and 30 cm from about $812 for the same area. Two qualifying 50 cm orders would start at $600 before analysis. The general archive minimum is 1 km². New orders generally start at 25 km² and some products charge for a larger fixed frame. Ask for the price of the actual dates, rights, priority and cloud terms. Free Sentinel-2 data can screen large works. [2] [3] [7]

costs.headline: Integration and operations require a quotation
costs.unit: USD · one optical payload on a compatible host · November 2026
costs.detail: No public price for a hosted submeter system meeting this brief was identified. DLR’s DESIS flew on the ISS using the MUSES platform. It demonstrates the hosting arrangement for an optical instrument. Request separate prices for the camera, qualification, integration, launch allocation, pointing time, downlink and ground processing. Contract duration, minimum commitment and rights need to be agreed with the host. [6]

costs.headline: Obtain a complete mission bid
costs.unit: USD · one spacecraft plus launch and operations · November 2026
costs.detail: A purpose-built submeter mission has no verified turnkey price here. For historical scale, NASA’s inspector general listed $839 million as the planned life-cycle cost of Landsat 9 in 2021. NASA’s 2017 launch award announcement put launch and related costs at about $153.8 million. The figures overlap and concern a different public mission. A construction-imaging bid should itemize the optical payload, bus, testing, launch, ground segment, operations and disposal. [9] [10]

markets.reason: AIIB showed Line R6 construction in Bengaluru. A lender or implementing agency could use the same sequence to ask where a surface milestone needs an independent check. Underground tunneling requires other evidence. [1] [4]

ESA published Sentinel-2 observations of the development of Beijing Daxing International Airport from 2016 to 2019. The sequence demonstrates the scale at which a terminal site and runway layout become visible in open data. Individual work packages may still require finer imagery. [11]

providers.name: Copernicus Sentinel-2
providers.text: Its multispectral imager records 13 bands at 10, 20 and 60 m sampling. Use its archive to establish when large earthworks began or expanded. ESA’s Daxing sequence shows what that looks like on a real site. [7] [11]

providers.name: Planet SkySat
providers.text: The SkySat specification distinguishes instrument sampling from the final image grid. Request a representative scene at the planned look angle before agreeing a roof-edge tolerance. The SkyFi prices above are marketplace examples without a specific SkySat delivery commitment. [2] [5]

providers.name: DLR DESIS on MUSES
providers.text: DESIS was installed on the International Space Station in 2018 and completed commissioning in 2019. Its different scientific instrument illustrates shared spacecraft services and negotiated data rights. [6]

limits.title: A roof can conceal unfinished work
limits.text: A continuous roof outline can coexist with missing fire protection, incomplete waterproofing or untested equipment. Keep contractual acceptance and payment sign-off with the responsible engineer.

limits.title: A late image cannot establish an earlier completion date
limits.text: If the last clear image precedes the payment deadline and the next clear image follows it, report that interval. Use dated field records to narrow it. Keep cloud-covered sections explicitly unobserved. [2]

limits.title: An apparent shift may be geometry
limits.text: Compare roof and ground edges separately. A fixed ground reference may align perfectly while a tall roof appears displaced. If the apparent change is comparable to the registration uncertainty, request a closer-to-vertical view or a field photograph. [5]

pilot.title: Replay one payment cycle
pilot.text: Pick one station or terminal and ten observable work packages with dated plans. Reserve signed inspection records for a blind comparison. Give the analyst only information available by the original reporting deadline.

pilot.title: Report the denominator
pilot.text: For an illustrative 6,000 m² planned roof, suppose 4,200 m² visibly has covering, 1,200 m² is visibly open and 600 m² is obscured. Report 70% confirmed covered and 10% unobserved. Do not count obscured bays as finished. Record the measured alignment error alongside the area estimate.

pilot.title: Compare the decision and the cost
pilot.text: Count correctly flagged discrepancies, false alarms, missed incomplete packages, unknowns and days gained before inspection. Compare with the engineer’s original review. For illustration, four analyst days at an assumed $650/day plus two new collections at the advertised $300 floor gives $3,200 before site visits, taxes, premium rights or repeat collections. Use actual supplier terms and internal day rates for the buying decision. [2] [3]

conclusion: Start with a milestone the owner can define on a drawing and an inspector can verify on site. Buy a dated image pair only when it can change a specific inspection decision.

hero.caption: Berlin Brandenburg airport during construction in 2019. The terminal roof and paved apron are visible from above. Systems inside the terminal need separate inspection.

evidence.title: Terminal 3 at Beijing Capital International Airport
evidence.alt: Satellite image of the branching roof of Terminal 3 and its surrounding apron at Beijing Capital International Airport.
evidence.caption: A 2014 Planet image of Terminal 3 at Beijing Capital shows a roof outline that can be traced against a plan. This is an example of a visible feature at a completed airport.
evidence.credit: Planet Labs Inc. Resized and converted to WebP.
